item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports learning recommendation-specific text representations, but the retrieved studies do not directly validate a lightweight, randomly initialized title/description encoder jointly trained with GRU4Rec. [Recformer (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) models item attributes as text and combines language understanding with recommendation training; its Transformer architecture and pretraining differ from this setting. [MARS (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) uses attribute-aware representations and attribute-wise matching, motivating separate treatment of title and description rather than indiscriminate concatenation. [TASTE (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14029) reports reduced popularity bias through text matching, providing related evidence about recommendations beyond popular items, without establishing the same benefit for a from-scratch GRU encoder.\n\nA compatible experimental hypothesis is one GRU4Rec network with randomly initialized token embeddings, separate masked-mean title/description pooling, and a small projection or gate combining text with item-ID embeddings. Train all components jointly on next-item prediction and use the resulting item representation for candidate scoring; retain one checkpoint and one scoring function per category. This is an architectural proposal inferred from the literature, not a demonstrated result. Compare against the corrected ID-only baseline using the pinned macro validation HR@10, with diagnostic breakdowns by training-item frequency and metadata availability. Text overlap can distinguish variants but can also over-rank substitutes; improved semantic similarity alone does not establish sequential compatibility or complementary value."}
